title: Field demonstration of a self-contained 10 km mobile-to-ground quantum network node via common-aperture co-propagation
authors: Dongkyu Kim, Dong-Gil Im, Kyungdeuk Park, Jisu Kim, Jonguk Choi, Yonggi Jo, Yong Sup Ihn
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a dual-function, common-aperture free-space optical system that simultaneously supports decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution (QKD) at 803 nm and bidirectional classical laser communication at 640/660 nm over a 10.31 km terrestrial link from a mobile platform to a stationary ground station. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first field demonstration of a fully integrated common-aperture architecture where a co-propagating classical optical link simultaneously performs full QKD post-processing and ecrypted payload transmission over a 10 km atmospheric channel. The classical link utilizes Manchester-coded on-off keying (MC-OOK) at 10 MHz, achieving a packet error rate of $\sim$ 0.4 $\%$ (estimated bit error rate (BER) of 3.13 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$) with hardware-based self-synchronization and error-packet retransmission. Over the 10.31 km link, the QKD system achieved an average quantum bit error rate (QBER) of 2.512 $\%$ and an average secret key rate of 644 bps using rate-adaptive low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Finally, using the distilled keys, real-time AES-256 encrypted image transmission was executed over the co-aligned classical optical channel, proving the feasibility of a completely self-contained, jam resistant mobile quantum optical network.
summary: This paper reports the field demonstration of a self-contained quantum network node operating over a 10 km free-space link. It achieves simultaneous operation of quantum key distribution (QKD) and high-speed classical data transmission using a novel common-aperture co-propagation technique. The success validates the feasibility of robust, jam-resistant quantum communication for mobile platforms.
main_problem: The paper demonstrates the feasibility of a fully integrated, self-contained quantum network node capable of simultaneously performing Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and classical encrypted data transmission over a long-distance, mobile-to-ground free-space optical link.
main_result: They successfully achieved end-to-end operation over a 10.31 km link, demonstrating real-time AES-256 encrypted image transmission using distilled quantum keys, proving a robust, jam-resistant network.
method: The system uses a common-aperture co-propagation architecture to transmit quantum signals (803 nm, BB84 protocol) and classical data (640/660 nm) simultaneously over the atmospheric channel.
model_or_system: The physical system is a mobile-to-ground free-space optical link spanning 10.31 km. It integrates decoy-state BB84 QKD with a classical link using Manchester-coded on-off keying (MC-OOK) at 10 MHz, all sharing a common optical aperture.
key_observables: Average Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) of 2.512%; average secret key rate of 644 bps; classical Packet Error Rate (PER) of $\sim 0.4\%$.
important_parameters: Link Distance: 10.31 km; Quantum Wavelength: 803 nm; Classical Wavelengths: 640/660 nm; Classical Data Rate: 10 MHz.
main_assumptions: The security analysis relies on assuming a basis-independent acceptance filter and uses mixture-martingale bounds for finite-key parameter estimation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the schematic setup showing the mobile transmitter and ground receiver sharing a common aperture for both quantum and classical channels. Figure 2 demonstrates the end-to-end process, showing the original image, encrypted version, and successfully decrypted image.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, covering both the quantum channel (BB84, filtering, detection) and the classical channel (MC-OOK, synchronization). It then presents the key performance metrics, including QKD post-processing (reconciliation, error correction, privacy amplification) and concludes with the successful demonstration of encrypted data transfer.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum networks, demonstrating practical, field-deployable integration of quantum key distribution with classical communication over atmospheric links, which is a major engineering challenge in quantum information science.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic and experimental setup of the 10 km mobile-to-station free-space QKD and classical optical communication system. Photographs and layouts of the vehicle-mounted transmitter (left) and the tower-based receiver (right). The 803 nm decoy-state BB84 quantum channel and 660/640 nm bidirectional classical link share a common aperture for key generation, post-processing, and encrypted data transmission.

FIG. 2. Demonstration of tactical image encryption, transmission, and decryption using the distributed quantum keys across the 10.31 km optical link. The panel illustrates the original vehicle image (left), the noise-like encrypted image with header preservation (center), the byte-frequency histograms of the correlated plaintext and uniformly distributed cipertext (bottom), and the decrypted image restored at the receiver (right).
